text: Theoretical economics is a fundamental discipline of economics, with the core goal of exploring the essential laws of economic phenomena and constructing a logically rigorous theoretical system. It focuses on studying the internal mechanisms of economic activities from an abstract perspective and does not directly target specific application scenarios. Instead, it provides a theoretical foundation for disciplines such as applied economics and management. Its research methods mainly consist of logical deduction, mathematical modeling and analysis of intellectual history. By constructing idealized models (such as perfectly competitive markets and general equilibrium theory), it explains the underlying logic of economic operation. It is the source of innovation in economic theory and also a "thinking tool" for understanding real economic problems.
